reviews.comment: Lectures often skipped important steps and moved straight to final answers, which made new material difficult to follow. Reviews were extremely long and still did not feel representative of the exams. Quiz corrections happened multiple times during the semester. I personally felt like I was fighting just to pass rather than truly learn the material
Class was made unreasonably difficult. Lectures were basically empty by the end of the semester because about 1/3 of the class dropped.

I would avoid this professor at all costs. This professor made the class a million times harder than it needed to be. He didn't realize that he supposed to be teaching the engineering version of the class and gave grad level exams meant for math students where the class average was a failing grade.

Didn't post notes online, if you didn't go to class don't expect to pass, even if you did go to class he would breeze through explanations like everyone should know how to do them. Did not explain anything with clarity. For exams just remember to breathe when he sticks it in you.

Paul was really nice and considerate. He was willing to allow extensions and accommodations. His class is very conceptual and pretty difficult, especially w/o sleep early in the morning, but I managed with the curve. HW can be long/hard without outside resources. Use book for quizzes and study his quizzes for MC, grind the review for FRQ.

Homeworks were tough and made you think about the material and apply to new problems. Past hw 8 they started getting really really tough but its a completion grade anyways. Tests were not terribly difficult, but he doesnt tell you exactly what will be on them which raises the difficulty level a bit. Good lectures but no posted slides so show up
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Funny guy. What wasn't funny was his lectures, his homework, or his exams. His lectures were confusing, never went through his thought process for example problems. His homework basically asked you to derive concepts on your own. He didn't have any practice exams just a review, so you had no idea what to expect on the exam. Review all HWs before.

Weekly completion grades on homeworks and quizzes. The exams are very difficult and almost completely theoretical questions. The lectures are not very understandable, but he is not the worst professor ever.

he knows the content very well, but his explanation is hard to understand because he uses lots of filler words. for the first exam, there was a topic that we did not cover yet in class. be prepared to spend at least 3-5 hours on each homework. since linear algebra is concept heavy, weird phrasings on homework and exams were very confusing.

During lecture he goes over the basic stuff, then the HW is impossible to do without chat. He doesn't care if you get a bad grade, but he is accessible during his office hours and teaches much better than in class. He moves deadlines all the time to help us. He doesn't post notes or anything so you have to go to class. He grades tests wrong tho.

The positives are he tries his best, and is very open to questions. The homework/quizzes are nearly impossible without chat, or office hours. Most problems are poorly worded, involve ideas not learned in class, or are far more difficult than what is discussed during lecture. Tests are hard because of how confusing/unhelpful the homework is.

IF YOU GET HIM DROP HIM IMMEDIATELY!!!! During the lectures when anyone would ask a question, he would seem annoyed and pissed and make remarks that made students feel bad fro asking a question. I felt so scared to ask questions because it seemed like we were bothering him. The exams are insanely difficult, he grades insanely harsh.

He genuinely likes what he does and I highly recommend taking this class. Attend lectures , they are amazing and he loves what he teaches. It was at 8 AM and I still showed up. There is oral exams but it's honestly not bad, he wants you to learn and guides you through. One of my favorite classes I have taken- highly recommend !!

You learned how to memorize a lot. He's engaging and funny in lecture. He wants to help you learn. He likes when you answer/ask questions. Go to lecture. Go to office hours. Oral exams (his office, 1-on-1, answer questions on the chalkboard) but not as bad as I thought. He GAVE me a 100 on my final. 89.3 end of semester and he GAVE me the A.

He's a good person. Genuinely passionate about a topic, and if you need help you can go to office hours. Gives guides for the exams. Only weird part is exams are oral and you present how you would do the question while he challenges you. Genuinely wants to see you succeed.

I took Dr. Simanjuntak in Spring 2024. Reading the reviews here seem excessively harsh. He taught all of the material pretty well, everything made sense at the very least. He is very nice and clears up any questions you might have if you ask. The averages for tests are low but the tests aren't excessively hard. Great Prof, would recommend.

The other reviews on Paul are quite harsh, I thought he was a good teacher. The course itself is pretty difficult, and vamps up as the semester progresses. There is a lot of homework, but it adequately prepares you for the exams if you complete them yourself. Paul himself is a good lecturer and is clearly knowledgable regarding the content of Calc3

Paul is a nice guy. That, however, does not make him a good professor. He makes numerous mistakes when teaching and rarely teaches off examples used in the homework. You will be teaching yourself this course and studying countless hours for tests that are even harder than the homework. No reviews are given. Avoid him at all costs.
This prof. has unclear grading criteria and subjective grading for the frqs. Partial credit is given sparingly. Does not provide review material for exams. Do not take this prof for any course.

Doesn't post anything, HW took VERY long (4-5 hours) but graded easy, only posts test review before exams (no other practice/study material/previous exams, but its similar to the test) but no answer key. The TAs grade hard, so he'll give back points on the test. Linear is a difficult subject, so having a good prof rly matters. GO TO OFFICE HOURS
Would teach the class well but made it more complicated than it should've been. It went downhill after exam 1

Linear algebra is a tough course and this was his first semester teaching at A&M, but he was not bad if you went to his lectures and his office hours which were very accessible. He did teach one whole lecture wrong which he later fixed, but he is funny and his reviews are good. He insists he is teaching Cal 3 tho which he will probably be better at

This class was extremely difficult. Each hw takes ab 4-6 hours and much harder than examples covered in class. Exam averages were in the 60s, & he lowered the avg cutoff for a D to a 50 bc of how hard it was. Gives review guides w. no answer key & no practice exams. Didn't curve at all. You can learn the same material much easier w a diff prof.
This class was tough. Very tough. First math class where I didn't get an A, but that's because I wasn't trying hard enough, let's be honest.
